title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 23 (Public Offer and Private Placement)

content.overview: Section 23 sets out the permitted routes by which a public company or a private company may issue securities: public offer, private placement, or rights/bonus issue. Listed companies and companies intending to list must also comply with SEBI law.
content.glance: Identify company type; map the issue to public offer, private placement, rights or bonus; apply SEBI overlay where listed or intending to list.
content.study: Section 23 is the gateway for Chapter III. A public company may issue securities by public offer (prospectus), private placement, rights issue or bonus issue. A private company may issue only by private placement, rights issue or bonus issue and must not make a public offer. Where securities are listed or proposed to be listed, SEBI Act and regulations also apply. Current-law framing: classify company and transaction first; then apply the matching route and connected prospectus/private-placement provisions.

sections.heading: Public Company Routes
sections.body: A public company may issue securities by public offer, private placement, rights issue or bonus issue in the prescribed manner.

sections.heading: Private Company Routes
sections.body: A private company may issue securities only by private placement, rights issue or bonus issue; it cannot make a public offer.

sections.heading: SEBI Overlay
sections.body: Listed companies and companies intending to list must also comply with SEBI Act and regulations.

sections.heading: Link to Later Provisions
sections.body: Public offer engages prospectus rules; private placement engages s. 42; rights and bonus engage capital provisions.

examples.title: Public company IPO
examples.body: A public company issues shares to the public through a prospectus. The route is a public offer under s. 23.

examples.title: Private company public offer (invalid)
examples.body: A private company attempts to offer shares to the public. Section 23 does not permit that.

hypotheticals.question: Can a private company make an IPO?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 23 confines private companies to private placement, rights and bonus.

hypotheticals.question: Does listing intention change the analysis?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. SEBI law applies in addition to the Companies Act route.

distinctions.title: Public vs private company issue routes

misconceptions.trap: Any company may freely make a public offer.
misconceptions.correction: Only public companies may make a public offer under s. 23.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 23 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify company type. II. Classify the issue. III. Apply permitted route and SEBI overlay. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Company type; issue classification; route; SEBI applicability; precise relief.

examTips: Start with public vs private company.
Flag SEBI where listing is involved.
